title: Tail-resilient prefill prioritization and kernel affinity
creator: Marco Chen
description: Problem: Large-tail latency events persist under mixed workloads due to suboptimal admission ordering and mismatches between prefills and decode-time kernel choices. Goal: reduce p99/p999 prefill+decode latency by 25% for multi-tenant hosted API while maintaining throughput and not increasing average cost per token. Approach: implement an adaptive prefilling prioritizer that (1) classifies incoming requests by expected decode length and kernel affinity, (2) applies a lightweight elevator-style prioritization that gives short/low-cost decodes a speculative fast-path admission, and (3) defers or reshapes long-prefill items into reservoir buckets when contention is detected. Additionally we will build a kernel-affinity map that guides admission so prefills likely to use the same optimized kernel are batched together, reducing kernel warmups and improving overall GPU utilization.
acceptance_criteria: p99 prefill+decode latency reduced by >=25% on mixed demo workload compared to baseline
No >5% regression in mean latency or throughput on steady-state traffic
SLO: zero more than 1 minute of outage caused by prioritizer misrouting in staging
End-to-end e2e tests covering short-path speculative admission and reservoir reshaping landed and passing in CI
technical_notes: Admission policy components: token-length estimator (fast heuristic), kernel-affinity predictor (small model + static heuristics), elevator queue with per-tenant soft-priority, reservoir buckets sized by recent load percentiles
Speculative short-path: admit small decodes immediately to low-latency lane; if they exceed budget at decode, fall back to standard admission with graceful retry and preemption markers
Kernel-affinity map: per-model rolling histogram of observed kernel choices keyed by (model-version, max_seq, quantization), stored in approximate LRU cache on each routing node
Backpressure: integrate with existing slot-reservation API; prioritize eviction of reservoir items by estimated cost and age
Observability: add trace tags for admission_decision, kernel_affinity_score, reservoir_bucket_id and expose per-route p50/p95/p99/p999 for prefill and decode separately
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misclassification of long decodes as short could cause repeated retries and amplify tail. Mitigation: conservative thresholds with fast EMAs and kill-switch that disables speculative lane if retry rate > 0.5%
Risk: kernel-affinity map stale on model upgrade. Mitigation: detect model-version changes and clear / re-seed affinity map; fall back to heuristic grouping (seq length + quantization)
Risk: increased complexity of routing nodes. Mitigation: implement prioritizer as opt-in feature flag per cluster and start rollout to small fleet in staging
work_plan: Week 1: implement token-length estimator and elevator queue primitives; add unit tests and simple simulation harness
Week 2: implement kernel-affinity predictor and local cache; add integration with admission decision path; start internal e2e tests
Week 3: implement reservoir buckets and speculative short-path; run canary on low-traffic region; collect traces
Week 4: iterate thresholds from canary, add observability dashboards and alerts, run scale perf tests, prepare rollout plan
Post-rollout: monitor for 2 weeks, refine affinity map TTLs, integrate with Optimize recommendations
